findings.title: Refresh pinned protocol schema fingerprints
findings.why_it_matters: The end-to-end protocol test pins every advertised input schema. The new Zod conversion intentionally adds strict-object constraints and other generated schema details, so its current hashes no longer match the schemas served after a build; the contributor/CI all-tests command will fail before it can validate the change.
findings.suggested_fix: Regenerate and review EXPECTED_SCHEMA_FINGERPRINTS from the built Zod-derived tools, then run the e2e protocol test (or npm run test:all) to confirm the intended public schemas are pinned.
evidence: src/server/tools.ts:327-331 now advertises schemas produced by zodToJsonSchema; each source-derived tool schema has additionalProperties: false (for example, new_bpmn hashes to fdd48f... rather than the e2e expectation 021771...).
tests/e2e/server.test.ts:42-45 states that fingerprints pin complete advertised input schemas, and lines 501-509 compare every tools/list schema to the unchanged constants.
All 24 source-derived schema hashes differ from the corresponding unchanged expected values, so the single e2e test will deterministically fail after dist is rebuilt.

testing_gaps: tests/security/request-validation.test.ts covers strictness for top-level objects and position/size, but does not directly reject unknown keys in add_event.eventDefinitionPayload or its reference, timer, and condition children. Add representative runtime and advertised-schema cases so the stated strict-nested-object guarantee cannot regress outside geometry.
